gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: A technical-drawing-pen line runs through every Righteous letter, with thin steel rod bent into commanding, playful shapes. Noto Sans Palmyrene, a sans-serif with short ascenders and curves that stop short of closing, lets a longer read slide by without fuss.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans PhagsPa is a sans-serif with see-through c openings and only a gentle bump from small letters to capitals. gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Commanding is off the table, so call it fun: Righteous bends steel-rod strokes of matching visual weight into a loud display face. gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahla: Righteous swaps hairline joins for full-width stroke connections, so every letter looks like thin steel rod bent into shape. gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-sc: Righteous looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, commanding and a bit playful, with thin rod-like strokes throughout. Noto Sans SC, a sans-serif with chalky open curves, answers with low-key ascenders.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Wirelike, fun and loud: that is Righteous, every stroke one thickness. Noto Sans Soyombo, a sans-serif with a sizable x-height and wide, unclosed curves, makes screen reading feel easy by comparison.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Righteous cuts horizontals and verticals at identical thickness, like rod stock bent into a fun, commanding display face. gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tc: Approachable describes Noto Sans TC, a sans with tall, large-countered a, e and s. Righteous holds stroke widths steady from stem to curve, so the body's outward-opening curves feel like a long exhale after the heading's bent steel rod.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Cut-out strokes like a fixed-width router bit give Righteous its commanding, playful steel-rod look. Noto Sans Telugu, a plain sans with a high-set midline and counters that stay open to the outside, does the quieter job of carrying the text.
